clue.text: Where they wash French articles without water

parts.note: la is the French feminine definite article, 'the'
un is the French masculine indefinite article, 'a'
something without water is dry

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that French items are somehow washed without any water.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundry is the room or business where clothes and linen are washed.

indicators.note: foolish suggests the words are being treated nonsensically, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reports a remark by Edgar Allan Poe calling a person fat and foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the technical adjective for fatty body tissue, so it means fat.

parts.note: reads as 'only just able to be seen', but means visible in a bare state, with no clothes on

explanation.surface: Something can only just be made out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seen without clothes is on view in the bare state, i.e. unclothed.

clue.text: Denial of fault in the show ring

definitions.meaning: a denial is a turning down of a request
in show jumping a horse that stops at a fence is penalised for this fault

explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a no to a request, and in show jumping it is a horse balking at a fence.

parts.note: sounds like a team holding a sporting trophy, but means the little dishes that teacups sit on

explanation.surface: A question about which team currently holds the trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Saucers are the small plates on which cups of tea or coffee rest.

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud or strong
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: An investor insists on backing a powerful business.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to state firmly or maintain that something is true.

clue.text: Ascertain unusual view of a philosopher

definitions.note: an adjective, describing the outlook of a particular thinker

indicators.note: unusual tells us the word is to be made into something different, an anagram

explanation.surface: A student is told to find out an odd opinion held by some thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartesian describes the ideas of René Descartes, the French philosopher.

definitions.meaning: a newly issued record or album
an instruction to let go or set loose

explanation.definitionFit: A release is a newly issued record, and to release is to set free.

clue.text: Check for mortar to be used in fortification

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
taken as written
cement is a mortar used in building

explanation.surface: A builder checks what kind of mortar to use when making defensive walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinforcement is the strengthening of a structure, much as fortification strengthens a defence.

parts.note: reads as delicate carpentry, but means a torch carried in old streets that also joins things

explanation.surface: A question about lightweight carpentry work.
explanation.walkthrough: A link was once a flaming torch carried to light the way, and a link is also a connecting piece, hence 'joinery'.
explanation.definitionFit: A link was an old torch giving light, and a link is something that joins one thing to another.

clue.text: A fight, but nobody is charged

definitions.meaning: a brawl in which everyone joins in
no one has to pay: admission open to everybody at no cost

explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a general brawl, and literally an event at no charge to anyone.

indicators.note: when speaking points to how the word is pronounced, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: to hoard is to gather and store things up

explanation.surface: An orator draws great crowds whenever he speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Hordes are large, unruly crowds of people.

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Superheroes might detonate a lethal device.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve gas is a chemical agent used as a lethal weapon of war.

parts.note: in business a sleeping partner invests but takes no active part; here it is literally a person one sleeps beside

explanation.surface: A question about a silent investor in a firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is literally someone who shares one's bed, and figuratively an associate.

parts.note: sounds like 'mad', but means no longer remembered

explanation.surface: Someone is described as crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has gone from memory, literally out of the mind.

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island
pen is short for penitentiary, a US prison

explanation.surface: An inmate thrives inside an American jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripen is to mature and come to full development, so to flourish.

definitions.meaning: to ... a hit, i.e. strike a target

explanation.definitionFit: To score is to hit or strike successfully, and a score is twenty, a number.

clue.text: Prevail over island uprising, being efficient

parts.note: to cap is to outdo or top

indicators.note: in a down clue uprising means the word goes up the grid, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Putting down a revolt on an island shows competence.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable means able to do things well, which is close to efficient.

clue.text: Freeloader surgeon prepared to accept credit

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other
prepared means made ready or worked into shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: A surgeon is willing to take payment on account from a sponger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgeon' looks like the subject of the sentence, but its letters are the raw material; 'prepared' signals the rearrangement and 'to accept' the insertion of the credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrounger lives off others, like a freeloader.

clue.text: Cover removers in action at start of cricket match

definitions.meaning: tools for taking lids off tins or bottles

definitions.text: in action at start of cricket match
definitions.meaning: the two batsmen who begin a side's innings

explanation.definitionFit: Openers are tools for opening lids and the batsmen who open an innings in cricket.

clue.text: A thousand accepted by university award, set up and developed

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so the letters read from bottom to top
accepted by means taken inside, so the thousand goes into the award

parts.note: a degree is awarded by a university
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A large sum is received by a university prize, which is then established and expanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' puts M into DEGREE to give DEGREME, and 'set up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerged and developed both mean came into being or took shape.

parts.note: nominally reads as 'in name only', but means literally by writing one's name, to join a job

explanation.surface: A question about pretending to take on a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign on is to put one's name to an agreement to work or enlist.

clue.text: A metaphor is mixed but its content is pithy

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a pithy saying

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the answer sits inside the words that come earlier

explanation.surface: A literary critic says that though a figure of speech is muddled, what it says is concise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters are found in a row in metaphor is mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphorism is a short, pointed saying, a pithy maxim.

clue.text: One of two — or one in three, perhaps

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the other
perhaps suggests the word could be arranged differently, an anagram

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzle about picking one from two or one from three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns THREE into ETHER, and 'in' places I inside it after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Either means one or the other of two things.

definitions.meaning: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting a fire or candle

explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to dwindle, and a taper is a slender candle or lighting spill.

clue.text: A habit that will keep one dry

definitions.text: A habit that will keep one dry

parts.words: A habit that will keep one dry
parts.note: sounds like a raincoat or monk's habit, but means a practice of avoiding alcohol

explanation.surface: Some clothing that keeps out the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstinence is the practice of refraining from drink, so it keeps one teetotal.

definitions.meaning: to call someone by name over a loudspeaker
a boy servant at a hotel or a court

explanation.definitionFit: To page is to call someone over a speaker system, and a page is a young attendant.

clue.text: It's beastly being a long time in one occupation

definitions.note: here meaning like a beast, specifically a lion

indicators.note: in tells us the long time goes inside the occupation

parts.note: a line of work is an occupation
an eon is an immensely long age

explanation.surface: A job that drags on for ages is described as horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, so like a beast, punning on the sense 'horrid'.

clue.text: Position of jockey produces a certain pace

parts.note: a stride is one measured step or pace

explanation.surface: A jockey's riding position produces a particular speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey sits astride a horse, with one leg on each side.
